name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
charge: Not serving the king’s gods nor worshipping the golden image which he had set up; not careful to answer the king in this matter: but if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods
summary: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image in the plain of Dura and commanded every people to fall down and worship it at the sound of the music, on pain of the burning fiery furnace (Daniel 3:1-6). Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom he had set over the province, would not bow, and told the raging king that their God was able to deliver them, and that even if He did not, they would not serve his gods (Daniel 3:12-18). They were cast bound into a furnace heated seven times over, walked unhurt in the fire with a fourth, and came out without the smell of fire; the king blessed their God and promoted them (Daniel 3:19-30).
offenseFull: Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold sixty cubits high, about a hundred and ten feet by the class’s reckoning, and gathered the princes, governors, judges, treasurers, sheriffs, and rulers to its dedication (Daniel 3:1-3). The study note likens it to the ribbon cutting at a new monument, and the Agree Together class calls it a one world religion, the same thing they are trying to do today, reading in class how evangelical pastors dedicated a towering gold statue of Donald Trump in Miami: Daniel 3 coming to life. When the music sounded all were to fall down and worship or be cast into the furnace (Daniel 3:4-6); the study note compares it to the national anthem at ball games, hat off and hand over heart, a form of worshipping the image of the eagle. The class sets it beside the image the whole world is made to worship in the last days (Revelation 13:6-8).

Certain Chaldeans accused the three men (Daniel 3:8-12). They were high up in the government, over the affairs of the province, and still refused; the verse by verse teaching contrasts the believer who goes to the job’s Christmas party so as not to be fired. The study note gives the reason plainly: they did not bow because of the law, which forbids other gods, graven images, and bowing to them (Exodus 20:3-5). Brought before the king in his rage, they were asked what god could save them from his hand (Daniel 3:13-15), talking big and challenging our God, though the teaching recalls he had already confessed Daniel’s God as a God of gods (Daniel 2:47). They answered that they had no need to answer him: their God was able to deliver them from the furnace and from his hand, but if not, they still would not serve his gods nor worship the image (Daniel 3:16-18). Whatever happened, they were never bowing.

The king had the furnace heated seven times more and his mightiest men bind them in their coats and cast them in, and the flame slew the men who took them up (Daniel 3:19-22). The Song of the Three Holy Children records Azariah’s prayer in the fire, confessing that all that came on the nation was true judgment for its sins, and that they had been given to lawless enemies and an unjust king (Song of the Three Holy Children 1:1-9). The class notes that even facing death they prayed for the whole nation, and that high office in the king’s government never made them call the enemy a friend.
judgmentFull: The flame streamed forty-nine cubits above the furnace and burned the Chaldeans it found about it, but the angel of the Lord came down, drove the flame out, and made the midst of the furnace like a moist whistling wind (Song of the Three Holy Children 1:23-27). The teaching says the fire did not simply get out of control: fire is a spirit created for vengeance (Ecclesiasticus 39:28-29), and the Lord killed those men. The king saw four men loose and unhurt in the fire, and the fourth looked like the Son of God (Daniel 3:24-25). The Agree Together class says the translators understood the fourth was Christ; the verse by verse teaching speaks of the angel who came down into the furnace, and the king himself said their God had sent His angel (Daniel 3:28).

The fire had not singed their hair or changed their coats, and they did not even smell of smoke (Daniel 3:26-27). The king blessed their God, who delivered the servants who trusted in Him and yielded their bodies rather than serve any god but their own, decreed that anyone who spoke against their God be cut in pieces, since no other god can deliver like this, and promoted them in the province (Daniel 3:28-30). The study note says he understood then that we had our own God, and that when the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the true and living God; the Most High is in the midst of Israel, and His people shall never be ashamed (Joel 2:27). The class warns that Nebuchadnezzar did not hold to it but went back to his idols, and that these events will occur again. The teaching’s charge is that nothing should stop us from keeping the laws of God.

text.text: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the princes, the governors, and the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

Then the princes, the governors, and captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, were gathered together unto the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages,

That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:
And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.

There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego. Then they brought these men before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them, Is it true, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, do not ye serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up?

Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, answered and said to the king, O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter.
If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.
But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his visage was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego: therefore he spake, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more than it was wont to be heated.
And he commanded the most mighty men that were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in their coats, their hosen, and their hats, and their other garments, and were cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.
Therefore because the king’s commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceeding hot, the flame of the fire slew those men that took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king.
He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spake, and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and come hither. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, came forth of the midst of the fire.

And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king’s counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.

Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.

Therefore I make a decree, That every people, nation, and language, which speak any thing amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill: because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort.
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, in the province of Babylon.

Then Azarias stood up, and prayed on this manner; and opening his mouth in the midst of the fire said,
Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers: thy name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore:
For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.

In all the things that thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment: for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.
For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.

Wherefore all that thou hast brought upon us, and every thing that thou hast done to us, thou hast done in true judgment.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king.
He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spake, and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and come hither. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, came forth of the midst of the fire.

And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king’s counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.
Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people,
And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king.
Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.
For the king had sent letters by messengers unto Jerusalem and the cities of Juda that they should follow the strange laws of the land,
And forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drink offerings, in the temple; and that they should profane the sabbaths and festival days:
And pollute the sanctuary and holy people:
Set up altars, and groves, and chapels of idols, and sacrifice swine’s flesh, and unclean beasts:
That they should also leave their children uncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation:
To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.
And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.
